issues.legal_issue: A holder of a superior proprietary interest in land is an intermediary even when under-proprietors manage the land and hold the direct settlement.
material_facts: The holder’s predecessor received an allowance connected to 133 villages settled directly with under-proprietors.
Revenue records shortly before vesting recorded the holder’s predecessor as proprietor of the village mahals and recorded the under-proprietors separately.
The holder’s interest in the villages had not been shown to have been extinguished.
issues.conclusion: The holder was a proprietor of the villages and therefore an intermediary in respect of them.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(8), 3(12) and 3(21) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 define an estate, an intermediary and a proprietor. A proprietor’s interest may be limited by settlements with under-proprietors without ceasing to make the land part of the proprietor’s estate.

predicates.vesting_allowance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a claim to continue receiving an allowance after land rights vested in the government.
predicates.recorded_as_proprietor: Revenue records identified the holder or the holder’s predecessor as proprietor of the land.
predicates.retained_proprietary_interest: The holder’s interest in the land had not been extinguished, although under-proprietors held interests in it.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an allowance claimed after vesting, and the holder was recorded as proprietor with a continuing proprietary interest, the holder qualifies as an intermediary for the land.

issues.legal_issue: An allowance linked to a proprietor’s continuing interest in land or its revenue is a land-related right that ceases when the land rights vest in the government, rather than a pension continuing outside the land reform scheme.
material_facts: The allowance was paid by virtue of the superior proprietary right in the villages and was varied at successive settlements as the land revenue and village assets changed.
The allowance was calculated in relation to each village, and the under-proprietors bore its burden.
Revenue records before vesting identified the holder’s predecessor as proprietor.
The allowance stopped after publication of the vesting notification, and the holder sought its continued payment.
issues.conclusion: The allowance was connected to the proprietary interest in the land, and that interest ceased and vested in the State upon publication of the notification. The holder could claim compensation under the Act, but not continued payment of the allowance as a pension.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4 and 6 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, an intermediary’s rights, title and interest cease and vest in the State upon publication of the vesting notification; section 27 provides for compensation. In State of U.P. v. Kanwar Sri Trivikram Narain Singh, [1962] 3 SCR 213, the allowance was a pension granted as compensation for extinguished rights, with no direct connection to the land or its revenue and no corresponding revenue-record entry. That case was distinguished because the allowance here remained linked to the land, its assets and revenue, and the proprietor’s interest.

rule.if: vesting_allowance_appeal and allowance_linked_to_land_or_revenue and allowance_varied_with_land_assets_or_revenue and land_vesting_notified

predicates.vesting_allowance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a claim to continue receiving an allowance after land rights vested in the government.
predicates.allowance_linked_to_land_or_revenue: The allowance was paid because of a proprietary interest in the land or its revenue.
predicates.allowance_varied_with_land_assets_or_rev: The allowance changed at successive settlements in response to changes in the land’s assets or revenue.
predicates.land_vesting_notified: A notification was published by which the relevant land rights vested in the government.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an allowance after vesting, the allowance was linked to land or its revenue and varied with the land’s assets or revenue, and vesting was notified, the land-related right ceases and the allowance is not continuable.
